mentions.heading: If we do not deliver new products, services, technologies, and customer experiences in response to increased competition, our business could suffer
mentions.detail: Start-ups, tech companies, ridesharing disrupt model; must commercialize EVs, AV, software-connected services, AI beyond core ICE business
mentions.quote: To successfully execute our long-term strategy, we must continue to develop and commercialize new products and services, including products and services that are outside of our historically core ICE business, such as EVs and AV capabilities, software-enabled connected services, future features and services based on AI, and other new businesses.

mentions.heading: Capital access needed to fund new technology development
mentions.detail: Technology development requires extensive capital; constrained or costlier capital versus peers could impair strategic plans
mentions.quote: If our access to capital were to become significantly constrained, if costs of capital increased significantly, or if our ability to raise capital is challenged relative to our peers, our ability to execute on our strategic plans could be adversely affected.

mentions.heading: Software defects and AI integration compliance
mentions.detail: Errors, bugs, vulnerabilities in vehicle software/hardware; AI integration may breach evolving regulatory standards
mentions.quote: Further, if we are unable to prevent or effectively remedy errors, bugs, vulnerabilities, or defects in our software and hardware, or fail to deploy updates to our software properly, or if we do not adequately prepare for and respond to new kinds of technological innovations, market developments, and changing customer needs and preferences, our sales, profitability, and long-term competitiveness may be materially harmed.

mentions.heading: Our ability to attract and retain talented and highly skilled employees is critical to our success and competitiveness
mentions.detail: Competition for software and hardware engineering talent for vehicles and connected services
mentions.quote: In particular, our vehicles and connected services increasingly rely on software and hardware that is highly technical and complex, and our success in this area is dependent upon our ability to retain and recruit the best talent.

mentions.heading: Our ability to maintain profitability is dependent upon our ability to timely fund and introduce new and improved vehicle models
mentions.detail: Development cycle of two years or more; EV acceptance depends on fuel prices, tax credits, infrastructure; high fixed costs
mentions.quote: The new vehicle development process can take two years or more, and a number of factors may lengthen that time period.

mentions.heading: Our long-term EV strategy is dependent upon our ability to profitably deliver a strategic portfolio of EVs.
mentions.detail: Must cut battery cell and pack costs, source battery materials, scale EV manufacturing; losses recorded on EV inventory including battery cells
mentions.quote: Our progress towards these objectives has impacted, and may continue to impact, the need to record losses on our EV-related inventory, including battery cells.

mentions.heading: The success of our long-term EV strategy is dependent on consumer adoption of EVs.
mentions.detail: Termination of U.S. EV tax incentives slowed adoption; EV realignment charges $1.6B and $6.0B in Q3/Q4 2025, $7.9B total in GMNA
mentions.quote: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we recorded total charges in GMNA of $7.9 billion. If industry-wide adoption rates continue to be slow, we may need to take additional portfolio actions to better match the consumer pace of EV adoption, such as not fully utilizing or reducing the capacity of our existing or future plants or reducing production hours or shifts, and we may become subject to claims by suppliers as a result of such actions.

drivers.name: consumer tax incentives for EV purchases

mentions.heading: Our near-term profitability is dependent upon the success of our current line of vehicles, particularly our full-size ICE SUVs and full-size ICE pickup trucks.
mentions.detail: Highest margins from full-size ICE SUVs and pickups; their cash funds EV, AV growth; oil price spikes could shift demand
mentions.quote: Any near-term shift in consumer preferences toward smaller, more fuel-efficient vehicles, whether as a result of increases in the price of oil or any sustained shortage of oil, including as a result of global political instability (such as related to ongoing conflicts globally), concerns about fuel consumption or GHG emissions, or other reasons, could weaken the demand for our higher margin vehicles.

drivers.name: full-size ICE SUVs and full-size ICE pickup trucks

mentions.heading: Fuel economy regulations could affect sales of high-margin vehicles
mentions.detail: Stricter fuel economy rules could limit sales or add material costs to full-size ICE SUVs and pickups
mentions.quote: More stringent fuel economy regulations could also impact our ability to sell these vehicles or could result in additional costs associated with these vehicles, which could be material.

mentions.heading: Highly competitive industry with historical excess manufacturing capacity
mentions.detail: High fixed labor costs, collective bargaining limits on closures; competitors' subsidized financing and incentives force GM to match, eroding margins
mentions.quote: In light of any excess capacity and high fixed costs, many industry participants have attempted to sell more vehicles by providing subsidized financing or leasing programs, offering marketing incentives, or reducing vehicle prices.

mentions.heading: Need for resilient North American-focused supply chain
mentions.detail: Raw material demand exceeds North American supply capacity; multi-year purchase commitments and higher inventory for ICE and EV supply chain
mentions.quote: Expected demand for these raw materials currently exceeds the North American capacity of the existing supply chain. If we are not successful in developing our North American supply chain, our results of operations and profitability could be negatively impacted.

mentions.heading: Low-cost manufacturers from China and India entering markets
mentions.detail: Chinese and Indian manufacturers competing in emerging and established markets, hurting pricing and share
mentions.quote: Manufacturers in countries that have lower production costs, such as China and India, have become competitors in key emerging markets and have begun offering their products in established markets, as well as low-cost alternatives to established entry-level automobiles.

mentions.heading: Foreign government protectionism and tariffs
mentions.detail: Foreign tax policies favoring domestic manufacturers and import tariffs could hurt GM and JV partners
mentions.quote: In addition, foreign governments may decide to implement tax and other policies that favor their domestic manufacturers at the expense of international manufacturers, including GM and its joint venture partners. Introduction or modification of import tariffs or tariff-related measures may lead to further challenges for GM and our global business.

mentions.heading: Refocused AV strategy on personal vehicles subject to technological, operational, regulatory and competitive risks
mentions.detail: Cruise robotaxi wound down Feb 2025; AV/ADAS efforts combined in GMNA; needs capital, AI talent, training data; competition from tech firms
mentions.quote: While we expect our refocused AV strategy to be less capital intensive than the Cruise robotaxi plan, we expect that our AV and ADAS development activities will continue to require significant capital investments and remain subject to a variety of risks inherent with the development of new technologies

mentions.heading: Regulatory and liability risks of AV commercial deployment
mentions.detail: Evolving federal, state, provincial regulation; accidents or cyber breaches of autonomous systems could cause liability and deter adoption
mentions.quote: To the extent accidents, cybersecurity breaches, or other adverse events associated with our autonomous driving systems occur, we could be subject to liability, reputational harm, government scrutiny, and further regulation, and it could deter consumer adoption of AV and ADAS technology.

mentions.heading: Risks associated with climate change, GHG emissions regulation and changing consumer demand
mentions.detail: Evolving emissions and fuel economy rules may require credit purchases or penalties, product portfolio changes, and raise ICE vehicle costs
mentions.quote: Despite recent actions taken by the U.S. federal government to reduce the stringency of emissions and fuel economy regulations, we expect such regulations at the federal, state, or local level or in international jurisdictions to continue to evolve

mentions.heading: Reduced emissions stringency slowing EV demand
mentions.detail: Relaxed emissions regulation has slowed and may continue to slow EV demand in North America
mentions.quote: In addition, the reduction in the stringency of emissions regulations has slowed and may continue to slow consumer demand for EVs in North America.

mentions.heading: Sustainability disclosure rules under legal scrutiny
mentions.detail: Shifting sustainability disclosure requirements may raise litigation, regulatory action and reputational risk
mentions.quote: Such regulations may cause disclosure requirements to shift and may increase the risk of litigation or regulatory action, which would result in increased costs (in our operations and supply chain), as well as risks to our reputation or consumer demand for our products if we do not meet demanding stakeholder expectations and standards.

mentions.heading: Climate change severe weather may disrupt production and demand
mentions.detail: Storms, droughts, wildfires may disrupt GM plants, suppliers, dealers, vehicle delivery and customer finances
mentions.quote: In addition, increased intensity, frequency, or duration of storms, droughts, wildfires, or other severe weather events as a result of climate change may disrupt our production and the production, logistics, cost, and procurement of products from our suppliers, timely delivery of vehicles to customers and operations of our dealers, and could negatively impact working conditions at our plants and those of our suppliers and dealers.

mentions.heading: Our business is highly dependent upon global automobile market sales volume, which can be volatile
mentions.detail: High fixed structural costs mean small vehicle sales volume changes disproportionately hit profitability
mentions.quote: Because we have a high proportion of relatively fixed structural costs, small changes in sales volume can have a disproportionately large effect on our profitability.

mentions.heading: Inflationary pressures and high prices and uncertain availability of commodities and inputs
mentions.detail: Steel, precious and non-ferrous metals, critical minerals, semiconductors and logistics costs raise production costs; may not pass through
mentions.quote: Increases in prices, including as a result of inflation and rising interest rates, for commodities, raw materials, energy, or other inputs that we and our suppliers use in manufacturing products, systems, components, and parts, such as steel, precious metals, non-ferrous metals, critical minerals, or other similar raw materials, or electrical subcomponents, including transistors, diodes, and other semiconductors, or increases in logistics and related costs, have led and may continue to lead to higher production costs for parts, components, and vehicles.

mentions.heading: Cost and availability of critical EV battery materials
mentions.detail: Lithium, nickel, cobalt, rare earth cost or shortage could raise EV costs and impede EV strategy
mentions.quote: In addition, elevated cost, or reduced availability, of critical materials for our EV propulsion systems, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and certain rare earth metals, may lead to higher production costs for our EVs and could impede our ability to successfully deliver on our EV strategy.

mentions.heading: Evolving automotive tariffs could materially affect results
mentions.detail: U.S. tariffs on vehicles, parts, raw materials; USMCA review; pending legal challenges; impact may exceed estimates
mentions.quote: New or existing trade agreements, including the ongoing review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, may also impact the tariff rate applicable to goods imported by GM or our suppliers. Additionally, certain tariffs are subject to pending legal challenges.

mentions.heading: Tariff mitigation may require footprint changes and charges
mentions.detail: Changing U.S. production plan and footprint may need significant capex, impairments, restructuring; won't fully offset tariffs near term
mentions.quote: We have made and may need to make additional changes to our global production footprint and workforce, which could require significant capital expenditures and could result in asset impairments and other charges, including restructuring charges, any of which could be material.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks
mentions.detail: China JVs hit by domestic competitors; $2.1B impairment and $2.0B equity losses 2024, $0.6B charges 2025; SGM further restructuring 2026
mentions.quote: As a result of certain restructuring actions previously announced in December 2024, we recorded an other-than-temporary impairment of our equity interests of $2.1 billion and additional equity losses of $2.0 billion in the year ended December 31, 2024, and we recorded charges of $0.6 billion in the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks
mentions.detail: U.S.-China trade tensions, weak Chinese economy, EV/software preferences and China supply chain integration may cut margins
mentions.quote: Increased competition, continued U.S.-China trade tensions, weakening economic conditions in China or China's level of integration with key components of our global supply chain, among other factors, may result in cost increases, price reductions, reduced sales, profitability, and margins, and challenges to gaining or holding market share.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks
mentions.detail: Chinese government may restrict investments or critical material exports with little notice
mentions.quote: The Chinese government may adopt new regulations that may impact entities operating in China or the ability of non-Chinese entities to obtain critical materials from China, potentially with little advance notice.

mentions.heading: We benefit from many joint ventures and strategic relationships over which we may have limited control
mentions.detail: Relies on JVs for EV battery cell manufacturing and raw material access; limited control
mentions.quote: If we are unable to successfully source and execute on strategic business relationships in the future, our overall growth could be impaired, and our business, prospects, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.

mentions.heading: We benefit from many joint ventures and strategic relationships over which we may have limited control
mentions.detail: EV raw material offtake agreements oblige purchases; low EV volumes or battery tech shifts could hurt cash flow; supplier investments may lose value
mentions.quote: If we are unable to utilize or otherwise monetize the raw materials we are obligated to purchase under these offtake agreements, whether as a result of lower than expected EV production volumes, lower than expected rates of consumer adoption, changes in battery technology that reduce the need for certain raw materials, or other reasons, it could materially adversely affect our cash flows and increase our inventory.

mentions.heading: Operations carried out by joint ventures with partners who may have different goals
mentions.detail: China and Korea operations, US/Canada battery and raw material JVs; primary China JV agreement expires 2027, renegotiation ongoing
mentions.quote: Our primary joint venture agreement for our China JVs expires in 2027, and we are in negotiations with our partner for a new agreement.

mentions.heading: Limited control over joint ventures and compliance
mentions.detail: Minority stakes limit control; JV misconduct, internal control issues could bring penalties, fines, reputational harm
mentions.quote: As a result, we may be unable to prevent violations of applicable laws or other misconduct by a joint venture, adverse human rights or other impacts, or the failure to satisfy contractual obligations by one or more parties.

mentions.heading: The international scale and footprint of our operations expose us to additional risks
mentions.detail: US-China tensions, dividend repatriation and technology export restrictions; FCPA exposure
mentions.quote: (5) political and economic tensions between governments and changes in international economic policies, including restrictions on the repatriation of dividends or in the export of technology, especially between China and the U.S.;

mentions.heading: Tariffs and trade barriers on global operations
mentions.detail: New or higher tariffs on products imported into or exported from the U.S.; free trade agreement changes
mentions.quote: (6) changes to customs requirements or procedures (e.g., inspections) or new or higher tariffs, for example, on products imported into or exported from the U.S., including under U.S. or other trade laws or measures, or other key markets;

mentions.heading: Any significant disruption at one of our manufacturing facilities could disrupt our production schedule
mentions.detail: Facilities model/market-specific with interdependencies; cannot easily shift production; weather, climate change, labor, health crises cited
mentions.quote: We may not be able to easily shift production to other facilities or to make up for lost production.

mentions.heading: Unionized hourly workforce under collective bargaining agreements
mentions.detail: Substantially all hourly employees unionized; agreements negotiated including at local facility level
mentions.quote: In addition, substantially all of our hourly employees are represented by unions and covered by collective bargaining agreements that must be negotiated from time-to-time, including at the local facility level.

mentions.heading: Disruption in our suppliers' operations could disrupt our production schedule
mentions.detail: Just-in-time minimal inventory except battery raw material offtakes; some single-source parts; could hit higher margin vehicles
mentions.quote: In some instances, we purchase systems, components, raw materials, and parts that are ultimately derived from a single source and may be at an increased risk for supply disruptions.

mentions.heading: Pandemics and other public health crises could materially adversely impact our business
mentions.detail: COVID-19 previously disrupted operations; could cause loan/lease defaults, lower auction pricing, impaired credit access
mentions.quote: Pandemics, epidemics, or disease outbreaks in the U.S. or globally, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, have previously disrupted, and may in the future disrupt, our business, which could materially affect our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity, and future expectations.

mentions.heading: Competitors may independently develop similar products despite our intellectual property
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Competitors may independently develop products and services similar to ours, and there are no guarantees that GM’s intellectual property rights would prevent competitors from independently developing or selling those products and services.

mentions.heading: Protection of intellectual property and infringement claims
mentions.detail: Trade secret theft attempts via IT intrusion, heightened by AI adoption
mentions.quote: We sometimes face attempts to gain unauthorized access to our information technology networks and systems for the purpose of improperly acquiring our trade secrets or confidential business information, and may face increased such risk from the rapid evolution and adoption of AI.

mentions.heading: Protection of intellectual property and infringement claims
mentions.detail: Targeted by patent enforcement actions including non-practicing entities; possible damages or injunctions on products
mentions.quote: In addition, we have been, and in the future may be, the target of patent enforcement actions by third parties, including aggressive and opportunistic enforcement claims by non-practicing entities. Regardless of the merit of such claims, responding to infringement claims can be expensive and time-consuming.

mentions.heading: Security breaches, cyberattacks, and disruptions to IT systems and networked products, including connected vehicles
mentions.detail: Connected vehicles, GM Financial data, third-party providers; cannot patch all vulnerabilities; acquired companies with weak security
mentions.quote: We are unable to comprehensively apply patches or mitigate all such vulnerabilities before they may be exploited by a threat actor. We have also acquired and in the future may acquire companies with vulnerabilities or unsophisticated security measures, which exposes us to potentially significant cybersecurity risks.

mentions.heading: Security breaches, cyberattacks, and disruptions to IT systems and networked products, including connected vehicles
mentions.detail: Reliance on vendors, suppliers, exchanges, clearinghouses and financial intermediaries for business activities
mentions.quote: We also face the risk of operational disruption, failure, termination, or capacity constraints of any of the service providers or third parties that facilitate our business activities, including vendors, suppliers, customers, counterparties, exchanges, clearing agents, clearinghouses, or other financial intermediaries.

mentions.heading: IT systems and connected products vulnerable to cyberattacks
mentions.detail: Regular phishing and cyber incidents at GM and third-party providers; threats amplified by AI; no material incident to date
mentions.quote: We and our third-party providers regularly experience cyberattacks and security incidents, such as phishing attacks, and we expect cyberattacks and incidents to continue in varying degrees, including due to the rapid evolution and adoption of AI.

mentions.heading: Security breaches and other disruptions of our in-vehicle systems could impact the safety of our customers
mentions.detail: Hackers have attempted to access vehicle software controlling engine, braking, steering, batteries; safety, liability, regulatory penalties
mentions.quote: However, hackers and other malicious actors have attempted, and we expect will attempt in the future, to gain unauthorized access to modify, alter, and use networks, vehicle software, or their systems to gain control of, or to change, our vehicles’ functionality, user interface, and performance characteristics, or to gain access to data stored in or generated by the vehicle.

mentions.heading: Right to repair laws could expose vehicle systems to third-party access
mentions.detail: Right to repair laws could permit third-party access to vehicle data and systems without adequate security
mentions.quote: Laws that would permit third-party access to vehicle data and related systems, including "right to repair" laws, could expose our vehicles and vehicle systems to third-party access without appropriate security measures in place, leading to new safety and security risks for our customers and reducing customer trust and confidence in our products.

mentions.heading: Enterprise data practices subject to increasingly complex, restrictive, and punitive regulations
mentions.detail: Subject to CCPA/CPRA, EU GDPR, EU AI Act, UK Data Protection Act; compliance costs rising, AI adoption intensifies risk
mentions.quote: Complying with these new laws has significantly increased, and may continue to increase, our operating costs and is driving increased complexity in our operations.

mentions.heading: Operations subject to extensive laws including vehicle emissions and fuel economy standards
mentions.detail: Fuel economy/GHG rules may limit profitable ICE sales, require credit purchases, penalties; unharmonized jurisdictions, possible sales mandates
mentions.quote: these regulations could require us to further limit the sale of certain profitable ICE products in current and future years, subsidize the sale of less profitable ones, change our manufacturing processes, pay increased penalties, purchase additional credits from our competitors or undertake other activities that may require us to incur additional expense, which may be material.

mentions.heading: Proposed GHG rule changes could impair emissions credits
mentions.detail: Proposed GHG standard changes could impair emissions credits, as with prior CAFE credit impairment
mentions.quote: In addition, proposed regulatory changes to the GHG emissions standards could result in an impairment of our emissions credits, similar to the previous impairment we recognized related to our CAFE credits.

mentions.heading: Limits on ability to achieve fuel economy improvements
mentions.detail: EV infrastructure gaps, battery raw material supply, consumer acceptance may prevent profitable EV sales needed for compliance
mentions.quote: There is no assurance that we will be able to produce and sell vehicles that use such new technologies on a profitable basis or that our customers will purchase such vehicles in the quantities necessary for us to comply with current or future regulatory requirements.

mentions.heading: Compliance costs and alleged violations of fuel economy or emission standards
mentions.detail: Alleged fuel economy/emission violations could cause recalls, fines, restricted offerings, facility idling; compliance costs not reasonably estimable
mentions.quote: Alleged violations of fuel economy or vehicle emission standards could result in legal proceedings, the recall of one or more of our products, negotiated remedial actions, fines and penalties, restricted product offerings, or a combination of any of those items.

drivers.name: fuel economy or vehicle emission standards

mentions.heading: Evolving regulation of advanced technologies including AVs
mentions.detail: Autonomous vehicle regulation evolving domestically and abroad; could impede commercialization and raise costs
mentions.quote: In addition, many of our advanced technologies, including AVs, present novel issues with which domestic and foreign regulators have only limited experience and will be subject to evolving regulatory frameworks.

mentions.heading: We could be materially adversely affected by unusual or significant litigation, governmental investigations, or other proceedings
mentions.detail: Product liability, warranty, class action, emissions, privacy, stockholder suits; see Note 16
mentions.quote: We are subject to legal proceedings in the U.S. and elsewhere involving various issues, including product liability lawsuits, warranty litigations, class action litigations alleging product defects, emissions litigations, privacy matters, stockholder litigations, labor and employment litigations, and claims and actions arising from restructurings and divestitures of operations and assets.

mentions.heading: The costs and effect on our reputation of product safety recalls and alleged defects
mentions.detail: Recall costs amplified on global platforms; AV safety concerns could trigger recalls and reputational damage
mentions.quote: The costs to complete a recall could be exacerbated to the extent that such action relates to a global platform.

mentions.heading: Supplier part quality issues and limited cost recovery
mentions.detail: Recall cost recovery from suppliers limited by supplier financial condition; defects may surface years after production
mentions.quote: Our ability to recover costs associated with recalls or other campaigns caused by parts or components purchased from suppliers may be limited by the suppliers’ financial condition or a number of other reasons or defenses.

mentions.heading: We may incur additional tax expense, become subject to additional tax exposure, or fail to fully realize available tax incentives
mentions.risk_name: Tax law change and incentive loss
mentions.detail: IRS audits; uncertainty over full realization of IRA incentives and law changes; deferred tax asset valuation
mentions.quote: the possibility of tax controversy related to adverse determinations with respect to the application of existing laws (for example, with respect to full realization of the incentives contemplated by the IRA), changes in our business or structure and changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities.

mentions.heading: We rely on GM Financial to provide financial services to our customers and dealers
mentions.detail: GM Financial funding via credit facilities, securitizations, debt; portfolio credit losses, used vehicle auction values, residuals, rates affect financing support for vehicle sales
mentions.quote: The primary factors that could adversely affect GM Financial’s business and operations and reduce its ability to provide financing services at competitive rates include the sufficiency, availability, and cost of sources of funding, including credit facilities, securitization programs, and secured and unsecured debt issuances;

mentions.heading: GM Financial must comply with financial services laws and regulations
mentions.detail: GM Financial subject to consumer protection laws; noncompliance risks penalties and license revocation
mentions.quote: The failure to comply with these laws could result in significant statutory civil and criminal penalties, monetary damages, attorneys’ fees and costs, revocation of licenses, and damage to reputation, brand, and valued customer relationships.

mentions.heading: Our pension funding requirements could increase significantly
mentions.detail: Plans hold significant equity and fixed income; discount rate declines or weak returns raise contributions; illiquid investments
mentions.quote: Future funding requirements generally increase if the discount rate decreases or if actual asset returns are lower than expected asset returns, assuming other factors are held constant.

mentions.heading: Non-U.S. pension plan funding requirements
mentions.detail: Certain non-U.S. plans have no assets; higher local minimum funding rules could strain liquidity
mentions.quote: Certain plans outside the U.S. do not have assets and therefore the obligation is funded as benefits are paid. If local legal authorities increase the minimum funding requirements for our non-U.S. plans, we could be required to contribute more funds, which could negatively affect our liquidity and financial condition.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical.
mentions.detail: Semiconductor capacity cycles cause overcapacity, high inventory, under-utilization and accelerated ASP erosion
mentions.quote: These downturns have been characterized by diminishing demand for end-user products, high inventory levels, under-utilization of manufacturing capacity and accelerated erosion of average selling prices.

mentions.heading: Significantly increased volatility and instability and unfavorable economic conditions may adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: 2020 automotive demand collapse from pandemic shutdowns; 2020-2022 rebound unmet; softening demand 2023-2025 from macro and geopolitics
mentions.quote: In the first half of 2020, demand in the automotive market steeply declined as a result of manufacturing shutdowns by automotive customers due to the coronavirus pandemic, resulting in an unforeseen negative impact to our results of operations.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly competitive; failure to introduce new technologies timely could hurt business
mentions.detail: Rapid change, price erosion, rising R&D costs from inflation; larger competitors and consolidation; need for on-device AI capability
mentions.quote: Meeting evolving industry requirements, including the increasing use of AI and machine learning technologies (including the need to run complex AI-based applications on devices), and introducing new products to the market in a timely manner and at prices that are acceptable to our customers are significant factors in determining our competitiveness and success.

mentions.heading: Risks from introduction and incorporation of AI technologies
mentions.detail: AI may give biased outputs, become obsolete, raise cybersecurity exposure; undeveloped AI legal landscape may impose costs
mentions.quote: In addition, AI and machine learning are still in relatively early stages, and the introduction and incorporation of AI technologies may result in unintended consequences or other new or expanded risks and liabilities.

mentions.heading: The demand for our products depends to a significant degree on the demand for our customers' end products
mentions.detail: Revenue mostly from Automotive, Industrial & IoT, Mobile, Communication Infrastructure; customers vary orders, postpone deliveries; custom products may be unsellable
mentions.quote: The vast majority of our revenue is derived from sales to manufacturers in the Automotive, Industrial & IoT, Mobile, and Communication Infrastructure end markets. Demand in these markets fluctuates significantly, driven by consumer spending, consumer preferences, the development of new technologies and prevailing economic conditions.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is historically characterized by continued price erosion
mentions.detail: Intense pricing pressure on older-technology products; may be contractually unable to cease production, bearing losses
mentions.quote: Moreover, we may not be able to cease production of such products, either due to contractual obligations or for customer relationship reasons, and as a result may be required to bear reduced profitability, or even a loss on such products.

mentions.heading: We depend on winning selection processes, and failure to be selected could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Lengthy bids with upfront design spend; automotive long design cycles can lock out a customer for years
mentions.quote: This risk is particularly pronounced in markets where there are only a few potential customers and in the automotive market, where, due to the longer design cycles involved, failure to win a design-in could prevent access to a customer for several years.

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: Tariffs on imports by United States and China, export controls and sector sanctions
mentions.quote: negative economic developments in economies around the world and the instability of governments and international trade arrangements, such as the increase of barriers to international trade including the imposition of new or increased tariffs on imports by the United States and China and other countries, enhanced export controls on certain products and sanctions on certain industry sectors and parties;

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: Middle East hostilities and Ukraine conflict affect customers, supply chain, energy prices and demand
mentions.quote: social and political instability in a number of countries around the world, including continued hostilities in the Middle East and the armed conflict in Ukraine.

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: China-Taiwan tensions, restricted entity lists could decouple trade and technology supply chains
mentions.quote: Sustained geopolitical tensions, such as the current geopolitical tensions involving China and Taiwan, could lead to long-term changes in global trade and technology supply chains and decoupling of global trade networks;

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: Coronavirus-type outbreaks affecting workforce, suppliers and customers
mentions.quote: epidemics and pandemics, such as the coronavirus outbreak, which may adversely affect our workforce, as well as our suppliers and customers;

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: U.S. dollar exchange rate volatility; transfer restrictions in mainland China
mentions.quote: volatility in foreign currency exchange rates, in particular with respect to the U.S. dollar, and transfer restrictions, in particular in mainland China; and

mentions.heading: Recently announced and future tariffs and other trade restrictions could materially and adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: 2025 U.S. tariffs and reciprocal measures; U.S.-China trade dynamics; April 2025 Section 232 semiconductor investigation expected to bring additional tariffs
mentions.quote: For example, in April 2025, the Department of Commerce launched an investigation into the national security impacts of imported semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. While the results of this investigation remain unknown, it is expected to result in additional tariffs and trade restrictions that may adversely impact our business.

drivers.name: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962

mentions.heading: Goodwill and other identifiable intangible assets represent a significant portion of our total assets
mentions.detail: Significant acquisition-related goodwill and intangibles; impairment triggers include IP validity challenges and regulatory changes
mentions.quote: Depending on future circumstances, it is possible that we may never realize the full value of our intangible assets. Any future determination of impairment of goodwill or other identifiable intangible assets could have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations and stockholders’ equity.

mentions.heading: In difficult market conditions, our high fixed costs combined with low revenue may negatively affect our results
mentions.detail: Own fabs incur full-capacity fixed costs at low utilization, as in first half of 2020
mentions.quote: During such periods, our fabrication plants could operate at lower loading level, while the fixed costs associated with the full capacity continue to be incurred, resulting in lower gross profit.

mentions.heading: We may from time to time restructure parts of our organization
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The costs of implementing any restructurings, changes or cost savings steps may differ from our estimates and any negative impacts on our revenues or otherwise of such restructurings, changes or steps, such as situations in which customer satisfaction is negatively impacted, may be larger than originally estimated.

mentions.heading: Failure to renegotiate collective bargaining agreements or consult works councils could harm business
mentions.detail: Collective bargaining agreements, social plans; works council consultation required for restructurings, acquisitions and divestitures
mentions.quote: We are also required to consult with our employee representatives, such as works councils, on items such as restructurings, acquisitions and divestitures.

mentions.heading: Our working capital needs are difficult to predict.
mentions.detail: Long development-to-delivery cycle drives high inventory and WIP; stockpiling across many specifications
mentions.quote: The comparatively long period between the time at which we commence development of a product and the time at which it may be delivered to a customer leads to high inventory and work-in-progress levels.

mentions.heading: Costs relating to product defects, product liability and warranty claims
mentions.detail: Software-enabled semiconductors; replacement costs exceed device value; customer recall cost recovery; personal injury exposure
mentions.quote: Moreover, since the cost of replacing defective semiconductor devices is often much higher than the value of the devices themselves, we may at times face damage claims from customers in excess of the amounts they pay us for our products, including consequential damages.

mentions.heading: We face risks related to security vulnerabilities in our products.
mentions.detail: Processors used in cloud, IoT, critical infrastructure and automotive applications; third-party IP and components also vulnerable
mentions.quote: As we have become a more data-centric company, our processors and other products are being used in additional and new and critical application areas that create new or increased cybersecurity, privacy or safety risks. This includes applications that gather and process large amounts of data, such as the cloud or Internet of Things, and critical infrastructure and automotive applications.

mentions.heading: Our business has suffered, and could in the future suffer, from manufacturing problems.
mentions.detail: Austin, Texas fabs disrupted by February 2021 winter storm; utility rationing of electricity, gas, water risk
mentions.quote: Further, we may suffer disruptions in our manufacturing operations, either due to production difficulties such as those described above or as a result of external factors beyond our control, such as the disruption to our Austin, Texas manufacturing facilities caused by the February 2021 winter storm.

mentions.heading: Reliance on timely supply of equipment and materials from limited suppliers
mentions.detail: Shortages of silicon wafers or specialized chemicals; equipment hard to substitute; tariffs may raise material costs
mentions.quote: Supply disruptions may also occur due to shortages in critical materials, such as silicon wafers or specialized chemicals. In addition, the imposition of tariffs or other trade restrictions may significantly increase the costs, and otherwise adversely impact the availability of certain raw materials and supplies needed for our manufacturing operations.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Could not obtain sufficient silicon wafers from foundry partners in 2022 shortage; unable to fully supply demand
mentions.quote: For example, as part of the industry-wide shortage of semiconductors during 2022 we could not obtain sufficient silicon wafers from our foundry partners to meet the demand for our products, causing us not to fully supply the demand for our products, and negatively affecting our results of operations.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Foundry prices vary with supplier utilization; costs rose significantly in 2022 shortage, pressuring gross margin
mentions.quote: Furthermore, these outsourcing costs can vary materially from quarter to quarter and, in cases of industry shortages like we experienced in 2022, they can increase significantly, which may negatively affect our gross profit if we are not able to increase the price of our products.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Long-term supply agreements with key manufacturing partners; supplier non-performance or demand drop could hurt results
mentions.quote: In addition, we have entered into long-term supply agreements with certain key manufacturing partners. The failure of these suppliers to perform under these agreements or an unexpected reduction in demand for these products could result in a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Disruptions in our relationships with any one of our key customers could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Substantial revenue from top customers including distributors
mentions.quote: A substantial portion of our revenue is derived from our top customers, including our distributors. We cannot guarantee that we will be able to generate similar levels of revenue from our largest customers in the future.

mentions.heading: We receive subsidies and grants in certain countries, and a reduction in governmental funding or demands for repayment could increase our costs.
mentions.detail: Receives government subsidies in some countries; curtailment or repayment demands if grant conditions unmet or operations terminated
mentions.quote: In such event that we don't meet the subsidies grant conditions, such government agencies could seek to recover such subsidies from us, and they could cancel or reduce other subsidies we receive from them.

mentions.heading: Natural disasters and climate change may negatively impact our business
mentions.detail: Factories in earthquake, flood or storm zones in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand; 2011 Japan tsunami hit supply chains
mentions.quote: The impact of any such natural disasters depends on the specific geographic circumstances but could be significant, as some of our factories are located in areas with known earthquake fault zones, flood or storm risks, including but not limited to Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia or Thailand.

mentions.heading: Climate change may cause more natural disasters affecting operations
mentions.detail: February 2021 winter storm disrupted Austin, Texas fabs and their water and utilities
mentions.quote: Such natural disasters pose physical risks to our manufacturing, IT facilities or our suppliers’ facilities, or could disrupt the availability of water and utilities necessary for the operation of our manufacturing facilities or our suppliers’ facilities resulting in increased operating costs and business disruption, such as the disruption to our Austin, Texas manufacturing facilities caused by the February 2021 winter storm and weather-related disruption of water and utilities to these facilities.

mentions.heading: Water scarcity in semi-arid manufacturing regions
mentions.detail: Water-intensive semiconductor manufacturing; many own and supplier sites in semi-arid regions vulnerable to drought
mentions.quote: In addition, semiconductor manufacturing is a water-intensive process. Many of our manufacturing sites and those of our suppliers are located in semi–arid regions that may become increasingly vulnerable to prolonged droughts associated with evolving changes to the climate, which may lead to water scarcity.

mentions.heading: Acquisitions and strategic transactions could adversely affect results
mentions.detail: Routine acquisitions, joint ventures, minority equity stakes and loans; integration of employees, R&D, systems challenging
mentions.quote: If we do not achieve the anticipated benefits of business acquisitions or other strategic activities, or if we are unable to consummate acquisitions or strategic investments that we consider important to the future of our business, our business and results of operations may be adversely affected and our growth strategy may not be successful.

mentions.heading: Government approval required for acquisitions
mentions.detail: Agencies have previously denied or delayed approval of transactions
mentions.quote: Certain agencies in the past have, and may in the future, deny the transaction or fail to approve in a timely manner, resulting in delays in closing and us not realizing the anticipated benefits of the proposed transactions.

mentions.heading: We rely on joint ventures to meet our current and future manufacturing requirements
mentions.detail: Manufacturing JVs SSMC (TSMC), VSMC (Vanguard), ESMC (TSMC, Bosch, Infineon); funding and take-or-pay obligations; ramp timing risk
mentions.quote: If we do not achieve the anticipated benefits of these joint ventures, or if newly established joint ventures are not able to begin production in the expected timing or achieve expected efficiency and quality, our business and results of operations may be adversely affected.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world
mentions.detail: U.S. EAR and EU sanctions; previously halted shipments to Huawei in 2020; new U.S. administration policy changes
mentions.quote: For example, in 2020, due to regulations imposed by the U.S. government, we ceased shipments of our products to Huawei pending approval of export licenses.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world
mentions.detail: EU GDPR and expanding global privacy rules could impose significant compliance costs
mentions.quote: Furthermore, global privacy legislation, enforcement, and policy activity, such as the EU General Data Privacy Regulation, are rapidly expanding and creating a complex regulatory compliance environment. Costs to comply with and implement these privacy-related and data protection measures could be significant.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world
mentions.detail: Dutch foreign investment control regime and U.S. outbound investment rules may limit acquisitions and alliances
mentions.quote: In addition, governments are increasingly imposing restrictions on cross-border investments in semiconductor businesses and technology, such as the Dutch foreign investment control regime and U.S. outbound investment rules, that may limit our ability to execute strategic acquisitions, investments and alliances, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: Legal proceedings are pending in various jurisdictions; adverse outcome might affect results
mentions.detail: Past claims of injuries to children of former employees from clean room chemical exposure; facilities operated by NXP or former parents Philips and Motorola
mentions.quote: For example, in the past we have been involved in legal proceedings claiming personal injuries to the children of former employees as a result of employees’ alleged exposure to chemicals used in semiconductor manufacturing clean room environments operated by us or our former parent companies, Philips and Motorola.

mentions.heading: Manufacturing operations are subject to environmental laws and regulations
mentions.detail: Strict, joint and several liability at current and historical manufacturing facilities; permits required
mentions.quote: Certain environmental laws impose strict, and in certain circumstances, joint and several liability on current or previous owners or operators of real property for the cost of investigation, removal or remediation of hazardous substances as well as liability for related damages to natural resources.

mentions.heading: Initiatives to address climate change
mentions.detail: Possible energy price increases, carbon taxes, carbon offsets and lower-carbon equipment and materials raising production costs
mentions.quote: Public and private initiatives to address climate change may result in an increase in the cost of production due to increase in the prices of energy, introduction of energy or carbon tax or the purchase of carbon offsets.

mentions.heading: Interruptions in our information technology systems could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Any significant interruption in our business applications, systems or networks, including but not limited to new system implementations, computer viruses, cyberattacks, security breaches, facility issues or energy blackouts could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Our computer systems and networks are subject to attempted security breaches and other cybersecurity incidents
mentions.detail: Has experienced cyber-attacks; AI-enabled phishing and malicious code cited as evolving threat
mentions.quote: We have, from time to time, experienced cyber-attacks attempting to obtain access to and misuse our computer systems and networks. Such incidents could result in the misappropriation of our proprietary information and technology, the compromise of personal and confidential information of our employees, customers or suppliers or interrupt our business.

mentions.heading: Employee misappropriation of proprietary technology
mentions.detail: Identified former employees' theft of proprietary technology, possibly violating export controls, reported to authorities
mentions.quote: We have identified instances of employee misappropriation or theft of certain proprietary technology by individuals who are no longer employed by NXP. In some cases, such misappropriation may result in the violation of applicable export control regulations, which we report to relevant authorities as appropriate.

mentions.heading: We may not be able to protect our proprietary intellectual property against improper use
mentions.detail: Patents may be challenged or circumvented; weak enforcement in some countries where it operates
mentions.quote: In particular, intellectual property rights are difficult to enforce in countries where the application and enforcement of the laws governing such rights may not have reached the same level as compared to other jurisdictions where we operate.

mentions.heading: AI technology intellectual property uncertainty
mentions.detail: AI built into products; IP ownership of AI unsettled by U.S. or foreign courts, risking loss of IP rights
mentions.quote: Finally, the intellectual property ownership and license rights, including copyrights and patents, surrounding AI technologies, which we are and may in the future continue to build into our products, have not been fully addressed by U.S. or foreign courts, laws or regulations

mentions.heading: We may become party to intellectual property claims or litigation that could cause us to incur substantial costs, pay substantial damages or prohibit us from selling our products.
mentions.detail: Possible treble damages in the United States, injunctions, product redesign or sales stoppage
mentions.quote: In the event that we cannot obtain or take the view that we don’t need a license, these parties may file lawsuits against us seeking damages (and potentially treble damages in the United States) or an injunction against the sale of our products that incorporate allegedly infringed intellectual property or against the operation of our business as presently conducted.

mentions.heading: IP claims arising from use of AI technologies
mentions.detail: Use of AI in productivity and products may trigger copyright claims amid uncertain legal framework
mentions.quote: Additionally, and in part due to ongoing uncertainties in the legal framework around AI, our use of AI technologies for productivity and in our products and services may expose us to copyright infringement or other intellectual property misappropriation claims.

mentions.heading: Loss of our key management and other personnel, or an inability to attract such management and other personnel, could affect our business.
mentions.detail: Dependence on senior engineers; competitive market for skilled engineers
mentions.quote: The market for qualified employees, including skilled engineers and other individuals with the required technical expertise to succeed in our business, is highly competitive and the loss of qualified employees or an inability to attract, retain and motivate the additional highly skilled employees required for the operation and expansion of our business could hinder our ability to successfully conduct research activities or develop marketable products.

mentions.heading: CEO transition risk
mentions.detail: Kurt Sievers retired October 28, 2025; Rafael Sotomayor succeeded as President and CEO
mentions.quote: Effective October 28, 2025, Kurt Sievers voluntarily retired as our CEO and executive director and Rafael Sotomayor succeeded Mr. Sievers as President and CEO and temporary executive director of the Company.

mentions.heading: United States civil liabilities may not be enforceable against us.
mentions.detail: Incorporated in the Netherlands; no US-Netherlands treaty on mutual enforcement; claims must be relitigated in Dutch courts
mentions.quote: In order to obtain a judgment which is enforceable in the Netherlands, the claim must be relitigated before a competent court of the Netherlands; the relevant Netherlands court has discretion to attach such weight to a judgment of the courts of the United States as it deems appropriate

mentions.heading: We are a Dutch public company with limited liability; stockholder rights may differ from U.S. jurisdictions.
mentions.detail: Dutch naamloze vennootschap; board must consider stakeholders including employees, not only stockholders
mentions.quote: In the performance of its duties, our board of directors is required by Dutch law to consider the interests of our company, its stockholders, its employees and other stakeholders, in all cases with due observation of the principles of reasonableness and fairness.

mentions.heading: Our debt obligations expose us to risks that could adversely affect our financial condition.
mentions.risk_name: High leverage and debt service burden
mentions.detail: $12,290 million aggregate principal debt outstanding as of December 31, 2025
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had outstanding indebtedness with an aggregate principal amount of $12,290 million. Our substantial indebtedness could have a material adverse effect on our business by:

mentions.heading: Debt obligations expose us to increased interest rates on revolving facility
mentions.detail: $2,500 million RCF restated to $3,000 million on February 6, 2026; variable-rate borrowings
mentions.quote: exposing us to the risk of increased interest rates in the event we have borrowings under our $2,500 million revolving credit facility agreement (the “RCF Agreement”), which was restated to $3,000 million as per February 6, 2026, because loans under the RCF Agreement may bear interest at a variable rate;

mentions.heading: Consequences of substantial indebtedness (continuation of bullet list)
mentions.detail: Leverage may trigger covenant defaults, restrict acquisitions, limit financing and create competitive disadvantage versus less leveraged peers
mentions.quote: limiting our flexibility in planning for, or reacting to, changes in our business or market conditions and placing us at a competitive disadvantage compared to our competitors who are less highly leveraged

mentions.heading: Despite our level of indebtedness, we may still incur significantly more debt
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Despite our level of indebtedness, we may still incur significantly more debt, which could further exacerbate the risks described above and affect our ability to service and repay our debt.

mentions.heading: If we do not comply with the covenants in our debt agreements or fail to generate sufficient cash to service and repay our debt
mentions.detail: RCF Agreement, EIB loan facilities and unsecured note indentures carry covenants; default could trigger acceleration and cross defaults
mentions.quote: The RCF Agreement, European Investment Bank (EIB) loan facilities and the indentures governing our unsecured notes or any other debt arrangements that we may have require us to comply with various covenants.

mentions.heading: Insufficient cash flow to service debt
mentions.detail: May need asset sales, refinancing at higher rates with more onerous covenants; dependent on capital markets
mentions.quote: Our ability to restructure or refinance our debt will depend on the condition of the capital markets and our financial condition at such time. Any refinancing of our debt could be at higher interest rates and may require us to comply with more onerous covenants, which could further restrict our business operations.

mentions.heading: The rating of our debt by major rating agencies may further improve or deteriorate
mentions.detail: Downgrades or review announcements could raise borrowing costs and affect market value
mentions.quote: Actual or anticipated changes or downgrades in our credit ratings, including any announcement that our ratings are under further review for a downgrade, could affect our market value and/or increase our corporate borrowing costs.

mentions.heading: The price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly.
mentions.detail: Closing price ranged from $245.86 (Feb 20, 2025) to $153.50 (Apr 8, 2025); possible securities class actions
mentions.quote: The market closing price for our common stock varied between a high of $245.86 on February 20, 2025, and a low of $153.50 on April 8, 2025, in the twelve-month period ending on December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: We may have fluctuations in the amount and frequency of our stock repurchases.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The amount, timing, and execution of our stock repurchases may fluctuate based on our priorities for the use of cash for other purposes—such as investing in our business, including operational spending, capital spending, and acquisitions, and returning cash to our stockholders as dividend payments—and because of changes in cash flows, tax laws, and the market price of our common stock.

mentions.heading: There can be no assurance that we will continue to declare cash dividends.
mentions.detail: Quarterly dividend policy; may be cut; restricted by law, contracts and corporate structure
mentions.quote: The declaration and payment of any dividend is subject to the approval of our board, and our dividend may be discontinued or reduced at any time.

mentions.heading: Impact of financial markets and demographics on defined benefit pension liabilities
mentions.detail: Net accrued benefit liability of $342 million at Dec 31, 2025 for plans in multiple countries
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had recognized a net accrued benefit liability of $342 million, representing the unfunded benefit obligations of our defined pension plans.

mentions.heading: Future changes to Dutch, U.S. and other foreign tax laws could adversely affect us.
mentions.detail: EU Pillar 2 directive effective 2024 enacted in Netherlands; OECD/G7 June 2025 side-by-side safe harbor may amend rules
mentions.quote: As part of the OECD framework to implement a minimum tax rate, the EU has adopted a directive on ensuring a global minimum level of taxation for multinational companies, also known as Pillar 2, which became effective in 2024.

mentions.heading: We are exposed to a number of different tax uncertainties, which could have an impact on our results.
mentions.detail: Transfer-pricing directives on goods, services, financing per OECD guidelines; cross-border disputes with local tax authorities
mentions.quote: As transfer pricing has a cross-border effect, the focus of local tax authorities on implemented transfer pricing procedures in a country may have an impact on results in another country.

mentions.heading: We are exposed to a number of different tax uncertainties, which could have an impact on our results.
mentions.detail: Tax assets from acquisitions and loss carryforwards may be challenged or require future taxable profits
mentions.quote: Tax authorities may challenge these tax assets. In addition, the value of the tax assets resulting from tax losses carried forward depends on having sufficient taxable profits in the future.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: About 60% of revenue from non-US-headquartered customers; China-HQ customers ~20% and shipments into China ~50% of 2025 revenue
mentions.quote: Revenue from end customers headquartered in China represented about 20% of our revenue in 2025, while revenue from products shipped into China represented about 50% of our revenue in 2025.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: US-China tensions; semiconductor-specific tariffs, export restrictions and sanctions could limit market access and equipment purchases
mentions.quote: Certain countries where we operate, particularly the United States and China, have experienced, and other countries may experience, geopolitical tensions and administrative measures that affect global trade and macroeconomic conditions through the imposition of tariffs, including tariffs specific to the products that we sell, import or export restrictions, trade embargoes and sanctions, restrictions on cross-border investment and other trade barriers applicable to the semiconductor industry.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: Generic statement on U.S. dollar fluctuations and remeasurement of non-dollar transactions
mentions.quote: In addition, our global operations expose us to periods when the U.S. dollar significantly fluctuates in relation to the non-U.S. currencies in which we transact business. The remeasurement of non-U.S. dollar transactions can have an adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: We face substantial competition that requires us to respond rapidly to product development and pricing pressures.
mentions.detail: Emerging Asian competitors; China promoting domestic semiconductor industry through policy and investment
mentions.quote: For example, we may face increased competition as a result of China actively promoting and reshaping its domestic semiconductor industry through policy changes and investment, which could prevent us from competing effectively.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Cyclical semiconductor market drives rapid demand swings across sectors
mentions.quote: The cyclical nature of the semiconductor market occasionally leads to significant and rapid increases and decreases in product demand.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Loss or curtailment by large customers due to sourcing changes, inventory adjustments, tariffs, export controls
mentions.quote: Additionally, the loss or significant curtailment of purchases by one or more of our large customers, including curtailments due to a change in the design or manufacturing sourcing policies or practices of these customers, the timing of customer or distributor inventory adjustments, changes in demand for customer products, tariffs, export controls or other trade measures, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Manufacturing forecasts for high service levels may cause excess or obsolete inventory, reducing margins
mentions.quote: Our manufacturing forecasts are based on multiple assumptions, and if inaccurate, could cause us to hold inadequate, excess or obsolete inventory that would reduce our profit margins and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Our operating results and our reputation could be adversely affected by cybersecurity events, breaches, disruptions or other incidents relating to our information technology systems.
mentions.detail: Could disrupt manufacturing and online services; threats include nation-state espionage and AI tools
mentions.quote: Cybersecurity or other threats to our information technology systems or the systems of our customers, suppliers and other third parties are frequent, increasingly sophisticated and constantly evolving, thereby making them more difficult to detect, mitigate and defend against.

mentions.heading: Our ability to successfully implement strategic, business and organizational changes could affect our business plans and results of operations.
mentions.detail: Generic statement on acquisitions, divestitures, capital investments and restructuring
mentions.quote: We may not achieve or sustain the expected growth, cost savings or other benefits of strategic, business and organizational changes, and charges associated with these actions could differ materially in amount and timing from our expectations.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be affected by natural events in the locations in which we operate.
mentions.detail: Principal manufacturing and design sites exposed to severe weather, geological events, epidemics; climate change may intensify
mentions.quote: Climate change might exacerbate these occurrences or cause natural disasters to occur with greater frequency and with more intense effects.

mentions.heading: Rapid technological change in markets we serve requires us to develop new technologies and products.
mentions.detail: Shortened product life cycles and ASP declines; R&D investments made before commercial viability assured
mentions.quote: In some cases, we might not realize a return or the expected return on our investments because they are generally made before commercial viability can be assured.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Supplier disruptions from quality excursions, conflict-free mineral access, credit market stress affecting supplier liquidity
mentions.quote: If our suppliers are unable to access credit markets and other sources of needed liquidity, we may be unable to obtain needed supplies, collect accounts receivable or access needed technology.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Key semiconductor materials sourced from limited geographies; geopolitical tensions and export controls on minerals, equipment raise cost and lead times
mentions.quote: Further, certain key materials used in semiconductor manufacturing are primarily sourced from limited geographies. Governments have adopted or proposed measures, including export controls on certain minerals, materials and equipment, that could adversely affect equipment and material availability, cost or movement.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Subcontracted wafer fab, assembly/test, advanced logic process development and facility construction; limited alternates, no long-term contracts
mentions.quote: We do not have long-term contracts with all of these suppliers, and the number of alternate suppliers is limited.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Ongoing manufacturing capacity investments under capital management strategy may not earn expected returns
mentions.quote: We have made and will continue to make investments in manufacturing capacity consistent with our capital management strategy, and we might not realize our expected return on those investments.

mentions.heading: Our continued success depends in part on our ability to retain, train and recruit a sufficient number of qualified employees in a competitive environment.
mentions.detail: Engineering, management, technical talent; international recruiting limited by immigration laws and policies
mentions.quote: Our ability to recruit internationally or deploy employees to various locations may be limited by immigration laws and policies, including changes to, or the administration or interpretation of, those laws and policies.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations and our reputation could be affected by warranty claims, product liability claims, product recalls or legal proceedings.
mentions.detail: Customer recalls of products containing TI parts, e.g., automotive and handheld electronics; insurance may be inadequate
mentions.quote: In addition, it is possible for a customer to recall a product containing a TI part, for example with respect to products used in automotive applications or handheld electronics, which may cause us to incur costs and expenses relating to the recall.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be adversely affected by distributors' promotion of competing product lines or our distributors' financial performance and operations.
mentions.detail: Under 20% of 2025 revenue via distributors carrying competing lines; distributor credit and administrative-measure risk
mentions.quote: In 2025, less than 20% of our revenue was generated from sales of our products through distributors. Our distributors carry competing product lines, and our sales could be affected if semiconductor distributors promote competing products over our products.

mentions.heading: Our margins vary.
mentions.detail: Owns much manufacturing capacity; capacity expansions raised capex and depreciation; tariffs, freight affect margins
mentions.quote: Because we own much of our manufacturing capacity, a significant portion of our operating costs is fixed. With our capacity expansions, capital expenditures and depreciation have increased.

mentions.heading: Our operations could be affected by the complex laws, rules and regulations to which our business is subject.
mentions.detail: Broad range of international, national, local laws; government inquiries could lead to enforcement actions or fines
mentions.quote: Compliance with these laws, rules and regulations may be onerous and expensive and could restrict our ability to manufacture or ship our products and operate our business.

mentions.heading: Environmental, safety and health rules affecting manufacturing jurisdictions
mentions.detail: Rules may require abatement equipment, material/process elimination, or energy/emissions fees; substitutes may be unavailable
mentions.quote: A substitute for a prohibited material or process might not be available, or might not be available at reasonable cost.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be affected by changes in tax-related matters.
mentions.detail: Facilities in over 30 countries; deferred tax assets realization at risk; tariff changes could affect tax rate
mentions.quote: We have facilities in more than 30 countries and as a result are subject to taxation and audit by a number of taxing authorities. Tax rates vary among the jurisdictions in which we operate.

mentions.heading: Changes in international tax laws including BEPS
mentions.detail: OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting laws' application to U.S. multinationals uncertain
mentions.quote: In addition, many countries have enacted or begun the process of enacting laws that align with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development’s Base Erosion and Profit Shifting recommendations; application of these laws to U.S.-based multinational corporations remains uncertain.

mentions.heading: Government incentives may be reduced or clawed back
mentions.detail: Received government and tax incentives for investments; subject to scrutiny, reduction, clawback or termination
mentions.quote: Such incentives could be subject to reduction, modification, clawback or termination, and such changes to these incentives could adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition and reputation.

mentions.heading: Our performance depends in part on our ability to enforce our intellectual property rights and to maintain freedom of operation.
mentions.detail: Claims from nonpracticing entities; customer indemnification obligations; licenses may be unavailable
mentions.quote: We, directly and indirectly, face infringement claims from third parties, including nonpracticing entities that have acquired patents to pursue enforcement actions against other companies.

mentions.heading: Our performance depends in part on our ability to enforce our intellectual property rights and to maintain freedom of operation.
mentions.detail: Unauthorized copying, cloning, counterfeit products bearing trademark; weaker foreign IP laws than U.S.
mentions.quote: Activities such as those listed above may affect our reputation and impede our ability to sell our products. The laws of countries where we operate may not protect our intellectual property rights to the same extent as U.S. laws.

mentions.heading: Our debt could affect our operations and financial condition.
mentions.detail: Debt securities with various rates and maturities; payments could divert funds or require refinancing or asset sales
mentions.quote: In addition, our obligation to make principal and interest payments could divert funds that otherwise might be invested in our operations or returned to shareholders, or could cause us to raise funds by, for example, issuing new debt or equity or selling assets.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations and liquidity could be affected by changes in the financial markets.
mentions.detail: Relies on bank credit lines supporting commercial paper and revolving credit facilities
mentions.quote: If we are unable to access these accounts and credit lines (for example, due to instability in the financial markets), our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected and our ability to access the capital markets or redeem our investments could be restricted.

mentions.heading: Material impairments of our goodwill could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Generic statement; significant goodwill on balance sheet
mentions.quote: We have a significant amount of goodwill on our consolidated balance sheet. Charges associated with impairments of goodwill could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.

risk_factors.name: AI adoption and regulatory risk
risk_factors.definition: Risk that the company's use of artificial intelligence produces flawed or biased outputs, increases cybersecurity exposure, or incurs costs under an evolving AI legal framework.

risk_factors.name: AI intellectual property ownership uncertainty
risk_factors.definition: Unsettled law on ownership of AI-generated or AI-embedded IP may cause loss of the company's IP rights.

risk_factors.name: Third-party intellectual property infringement claims
risk_factors.definition: Claims by third parties, including non-practicing entities and AI-related copyright holders, that the company infringes their IP may lead to damages, injunctions, indemnification costs or product redesign.

risk_factors.name: Autonomous technology development and competition
risk_factors.definition: Risk that the company fails to successfully develop and commercialize autonomous driving and ADAS technologies due to capital needs, talent and data requirements, and competition from technology firms.

risk_factors.name: Autonomous vehicle regulation and liability
risk_factors.definition: Risk that evolving regulation of autonomous vehicles and liability from accidents or cyber breaches of autonomous systems increase costs and deter adoption.

risk_factors.name: Capacity investment return shortfall
risk_factors.definition: Risk that investments in manufacturing capacity fail to generate the expected returns.
